subject.title: Memory system: Cannot delete stale memories, conflicting entries persist

question: Should OpenClaw solve this now by surfacing deletable UUIDs in `memory_recall` content, or wait for the broader memory lifecycle contract to define review, edit, forget, tombstone, and conflict behavior together?
rationale: The source-level gap is real, but exposing IDs, accepting numeric indexes, or adding replacement/deprecation semantics each creates a different model-visible memory cleanup contract.

options.title: Approve narrow recall UUID handoff
options.body: Expose the existing memory UUID in model-visible recall output and leave replacement/deprecation semantics to the broader lifecycle issue.

options.title: Fold into lifecycle design
options.body: Keep this issue blocked on the broader review/edit/forget/tombstone contract before changing recall output.

options.title: Choose a different deletion handle
options.body: Define a safer selector than raw UUIDs or transient numeric indexes, then update recall, forget, tests, and docs together.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow recall UUID handoff
recommendation.body: Expose the existing memory UUID in model-visible recall output and leave replacement/deprecation semantics to the broader lifecycle issue.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent memory-lancedb history and repeated plugin-area touches make this the best available routing candidate for the immediate plugin decision.
